newsitem.title: FINLAND: LOWER '97 GDP FORECAST DUE TO INVESTMENT VIEW - PSP.
newsitem.headline: LOWER '97 GDP FORECAST DUE TO INVESTMENT VIEW - PSP.

text.p: Economists at Finnish state-owned bank Postipankki Oy on Thursday said their forecast for GDP growth this year was lower than the finance ministry's mainly because they expect lower investment.
In a new forecast, Postipankki projected GDP growth of 3.8 percent this year -- 0.8 percentage points down on the finance ministry's 4.6 percent 1997 GDP growth forecast last week.

"We expect investment by big companies to grow rather slowly, and that most of the growth in investment will depend on housing construction," PSP chief economist Tarja Heinonen told a news conference on the bank's forecast.
Postipankki said it expected fixed investment to rise 4.7 percent this year, whereas the finance ministry's forecast is for 10.8 percent growth.
"We also expect home building to get off to a gradual start and not to happen as a big jump," Heinonen said.
Postipankki has recently been more moderate than other forecasting institutions in its predictions for construction, Heinonen said.

Postipankki's economists also pointed to other minor reasons for the discrepancy with the finance ministry's growth projection, including their slightly lower forecasts for consumption and inventories.
Postipankki expected consumption to grow 2.7 percent this year compared to the ministry's forecast for a 2.9 percent increase.
